blocks.text: Most introductions to neural networks start with equations. This one starts with a concrete problem, recognising handwritten digits, and only introduces **neurons**, **weights** and **biases** when you already know why they are needed.

items: A neuron is just a number between 0 and 1, its *activation*.
Each layer's activations are a weighted sum of the previous layer, passed through a squashing function.
Learning means finding the weights and biases that make the output layer match the right digit.

blocks.text: It pairs well with the [precision and recall](#/?item=precision-and-recall-without-the-confusion) article, which covers how to judge a model once it has been trained.
